liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (3 reviews): The Bird Song jam is described as very jazzy; Bird Song is called funky for early 1982 [19][20][21]
- **(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction** (1 review, 2 other sources): Bob going off in Satisfaction reliably makes the reviewer laugh; A false start to Satisfaction is kept in the Satisfaction track [1][3][23]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet into Fire is excellent, followed by a groovy Estimated Prophet [17]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Vocal harmonies during The Wheel are somewhat harsh [17]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Estimated Prophet is described as thoroughly grooving [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd82-02-17 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-02-17 s1t02 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-02-17 s1t03 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-02-17 s1t04 On The Road Again**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-02-17 s1t05 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-02-17 s1t06 CC Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-02-17 s1t07 Tennessee Jed**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-02-17 s1t08 It's All Over Now**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-02-17.144621.fob.nak700.streeter.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 176 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1982-02-17.138012.mtx.seamons.ht111.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 182 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd82-02-17.sbd-patched.warner.23221.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 180 min; rated 3.93/5 by 14 [4]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is very nice, though it contains a couple of audience-recording patches; Sound is great, though the reviewer wanted a bit more Phil in the mix [17][23]
- **gd1982-02-17.176853.nak700.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 176 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd82-02-17.aud-martin.warner.21916.sbeok.flacf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 175 min; rated 4.1/5 by 10 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the audience recording sounds great, with good atmosphere [18]
- **gd1982-02-17.163538.akg.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 176 min [9]
- **gd82-02-17.sbd.braverman.15033.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 170 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [11]. Said about its sound: All soundboard copies start Minglewood mid-line, partway into the opening verse; Soundboard has a bad cut in Tennessee Jed, after the last verse and before the long solo; Soundboard cuts Fire severely, losing the third verse and everything after it [13][14]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the Warfield seemed to always get Jerry going [19]
- Reviewer says the Warfield seemed to always get Jerry going [20]
- Reviewer says this show sounds unlike other 1982 shows heard; opening Minglewood into Sugaree and All Over Now are good signs [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-02-17.144621.fob.nak700.streeter.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Frank Streeter's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5M (TDK SA-90) [1]. Also: N. Hoey's Nakamichi 300 source supplies the crowd, first notes of Minglewood, and an 11:04 Drums patch [1]
- **gd1982-02-17.138012.mtx.seamons.ht111.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix of SBD (shnid=112408) and AUD (shnid=21916) by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16… [3]
- **gd82-02-17.sbd-patched.warner.23221.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1982-02-17.176853.nak700.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Bob Menke's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5 [6]. Also: Frank Streeter's Nakamichi 700 source supplies short patches in Drums and in the Satisfaction tease [6]
- **gd82-02-17.aud-martin.warner.21916.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Steven Martin; source: Audience Recording: Nak CM700's [7]
- **gd1982-02-17.163538.akg.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Wiseman and Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [9]. Also: Streeter's Nakamichi 700 supplies the first five songs, Drums patches, and a 2:46 patch in Sugar Magnolia [9]
- **gd82-02-17.sbd.braverman.15033.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [11]
